title: Bentley takes us for a ride in its new EV, the Torcal
gist: Bentley's first pure-EV, the Torcal (unveiling September 23), shares core engineering with the Porsche Cayenne EV and deliberately caps power below four-digit horsepower while using human-drummed synthetic engine sound to preserve brand emotional identity, showing how VW Group platform-sharing and 'authentic' EV soundscaping are becoming standard luxury-EV strategies.

insights.claim: Bentley's first battery-electric vehicle, the Torcal, shares 'quite a lot' of its basic engineering with the Porsche Cayenne EV, reworked by Bentley for its own needs, and targets similar range (300 mi EPA / 600 km WLTP) and 400 kW DC fast-charging.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Confirms continued deep platform-sharing within VW Group's luxury brands as the capital-efficient path to EV development, spreading R&D costs for expensive EV architecture across Porsche and Bentley volumes.
insights.quote: If the proportions remind you of a Porsche Cayenne EV, that's because the two share quite a lot of the same basic engineering, albeit reworked by Bentley to suit its needs.

insights.claim: Unlike the Cayenne's four-digit horsepower ceiling, Bentley is deliberately capping the Torcal at over 850 PS (838 hp/625 kW) and over 1,000 Nm (737 lb-ft) of torque, prioritizing 'effortless' linear power delivery over peak numbers.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Shows Bentley differentiating its EV positioning from Porsche not on outright power but on brand-specific ride character, a strategy to avoid direct spec-sheet competition with its sibling brand.
insights.quote: We'll be well over a thousand newton-meters of torque [737 lb-ft]... There'll be over 850 PS [838 hp/625 kW], but we're not chasing four figures.

insights.claim: The Torcal uses the same 48V dual-valve damper active ride comfort system already deployed on the Porsche Panamera, another example of cross-brand component reuse within the VW Group portfolio.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Further evidence of shared-parts strategy reducing incremental engineering cost for Bentley's EV transition.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Torcal might be Bentley's new entry point'

insights.claim: Bentley chose to recreate its 6.75L V8 firing order using live human drummers rather than sampling the actual engine, deliberately preserving the natural imperfections and tolerances of a real mechanical engine in the EV's synthetic soundscape.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Illustrates how legacy luxury automakers are treating engine sound as core brand IP that must be reproduced authentically in EVs rather than replaced with generic synthesized tones — a template other heritage brands (e.g., Aston Martin, Ferrari) may follow.
insights.quote: We chose to use artists, humans to recreate the pattern. So they play the firing order, the V8 on drums.
insights.locator: quote from Martin Page in section 'The beat of a drum'

insights.claim: Bentley deliberately avoided the loud external speaker approach used by Dodge on the Charger EV, keeping its synthetic engine sound subtle and load-mapped rather than a marketing gimmick.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A brand-positioning contrast point: ultra-luxury EV sound design is being treated as a subtlety/craft differentiator versus mass-market EV muscle-car sound marketing.

insights.claim: Bentley will unveil the production Torcal on September 23, positioning it as a new, shorter/smaller entry point below the Bentayga in Bentley's lineup.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete near-term catalyst date for Bentley's first full EV reveal, relevant to tracking VW Group's EV product cadence and luxury-EV competitive positioning.
insights.quote: Bentley will unveil the production Torcal on September 23.

insights.claim: The Torcal drops Bentley's traditional metal organ-stopper air vent controls in favor of digital, infotainment-screen-controlled vents, mirroring the Cayenne's approach and signaling a broader shift away from tactile luxury switchgear toward software-controlled interiors even at the ultra-luxury tier.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Even brands built on tactile craftsmanship are migrating physical controls to software/touchscreen interfaces, a broader auto-industry trend with implications for supplier mix (fewer mechanical switchgear parts, more display/software content).
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'One bit of Bentley character'
